Mutations in genes responsible for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (MPZ, PMP22, PRX, EGR2) disrupt the formation and maintenance of the myelin sheath, leading to peripheral neuropathy. Similarly, mutations in genes associated with Usher syndrome type 2C (ADGRV1, PDZD7) disrupt inner ear development and photoreceptor function, leading to hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction, and retinitis pigmentosa. The convergence occurs on the cellular machinery and developmental pathways essential for sensory organ function, specifically myelination for nerve signal transmission, and the proper development of the inner ear and retina.

falsification.text: Absence of pathogenic variants in MPZ, PMP22, PRX, EGR2 in individuals with Usher syndrome 2C, or absence of pathogenic variants in ADGRV1, PDZD7 in individuals with CMT type 3, would falsify a direct shared causal gene hypothesis.
